findings.detail: F5 now holds for GET /cases/{id}/risk only (rait-case-risk.service.ts:81-99 runs authenticate and a nonlocking assertCase(...,false) before raitLockRiskRelations). GET claim-context read() still calls raitLockRiskRelations(tx) as its first statement, before this.pools(tx, principal) authenticates the caller or checks pool eligibility. That call takes table-global SHARE locks on ops.parameter and inf.rait_holiday. So an unauthenticated caller, a caller with no eligible pool, or one whose pool_id is out of scope still briefly blocks parameter and holiday writers in every tenant. The same ordering was already there at dbb7f2b8 (line 231), so this is not a new regression. It is a remaining case of the F5 class that the correction did not reach. The claim-next dispatch (rait-case-command.service.ts:931) takes the locks before scope.command, but S2-R9 explicitly prescribes that ordering, so it is not part of this finding.
findings.recommendation: In read(), run the existing nonlocking this.pools(tx, principal) preauthorization and return 404/400 for denied, missing or ineligible callers before raitLockRiskRelations. Then keep the current locked flow and the existing finalScope equality fence unchanged. Inspector adds a sensor: a denied claim-context caller must not wait behind, or block, a concurrent ops.parameter writer. If the Architect rules that R7/R9 deliberately covers this GET ordering, record that instead of changing the code.

limitations: Static read-only review of the exact runtime delta dbb7f2b8..ca83c18d: rait-risk.providers.ts, rait-risk.port.ts (raitSourceRows batching, raitQualifyPolicy), rait-case-risk.service.ts, rait-claim-context.service.ts, rait-case-command.service.ts (shared Calendar, single fenced candidates call), deadlines rait-risk.ts, the generated commands OpenAPI/server/client delta, .prettierignore, and the fixture qualifyPolicy reader. I executed nothing: no DB, HTTP, unit, e2e, pnpm check or CI. All GREEN/RED counts cited are the implementer's reports, not reproduced here.

F1 was assessed as resolved at the source level. The optional C-only qualifyPolicy gets a deduplicated pair-shaped request: base case/AIT/infraction, C clock, T-PAR timer, the reset movement event and audit refs, plus the exact WF-RAIT-002.md#4.2 anchor and sha256. Result keys are strictly checked, receiptDigest is a separate sha256 field, versions are format-checked without decoding rrv1, and the follow-on full movement qualify passes [receiptDigest] as its dependency. The production reader has no qualifyPolicy, so C fails closed through catch to unavailable (503). The fixture's opaque versions deliberately differ from receipt digests. Fixture custody is test-only synthetic authority, not production or legal approval.

F2 was assessed as resolved. The provider uses RaitDeadlineEngineFactory.calendar(tx), the same object the engine now consumes. Ladder reachedOn values are raw addCalendarDays/addCalendarMonths. Rounding applies only to due/ceiling, with nextBusinessDay semantics equal to the old loop. The calendar inherits the existing calendar's lack of holiday-scope filtering; that is not a new algorithm.

F4 was assessed as resolved: evaluateRaitRisk returns sorted unique sourceVersions. F5 was resolved for the risk GET: the nonlocking S1 purpose check runs first, then the R7 relation locks and parent locks, then a locked same-Tx assertCase before snapshot. Both locking paths take inf.rait_case FOR UPDATE, so the reorder adds no lock-upgrade deadlock. Same-actor inversions between case and pool_member predate this delta.

F3 is still OPEN under the accepted R12 disposition. cursorKey is still process-local randomBytes(32) (rait-claim-context.service.ts:47). Cursors therefore fail after a restart and across replicas. No shared signing input was fabricated. This is a real delivery limitation, not full contract or deployment completeness.

R10 was assessed statically. One materialized READ COMMITTED statement freezes pools, members, potential cases (FOR UPDATE), routes and batches, using the same defense_previa and mandate predicates as pools(). Parent locks and qualification run once. A final nonlocking re-read must be canonically equal, otherwise 503 before effects. There is no second expanding lock pass. Concurrent route/batch changes and absorbed arrivals deliberately produce 503 instead of retrying. I did not observe concurrency behaviour.

R14 was assessed statically. Per table, refs are batched in sorted ordinal order through unnest WITH ORDINALITY plus a tenant predicate and RLS. Cardinality is exact, ordinals are deleted once, and output is re-sorted by sourceRef. Projections are unchanged: UTC microsecond timestamps, to_char dates, hex hashes, event_id::text, and (event_id, occurred_at) audit identity. FOR SHARE applies only to mutable tables; audit.events and the legacy qualification stay unlocked. There is no Number conversion, cross-call cache or physical-ID map. Every FIELDS projection includes tenant_id, so null-tenant rows are rejected as before. Bigint beyond the JS safe-integer range, missing schema and artificially ambiguous keys remain unproven, as stated.

The OpenAPI delta adds only an outer object with required code enum branches on six command error responses, matching the existing inner branches. The server-generated types and the one api-clients file are consistent. .prettierignore adds only work/rounds/R-0025/reviews/S2-source/prompt.md. I did not re-verify the R16 banner text against hashes.

The full 115-test HTTP census and the three off-page controls were not executed on the final runtime. The post-batching risk retry failed in protocol setup under host load (244 on 8 CPUs), so there is no final runtime GREEN. That gap is preserved as a limitation and is not inferred to be a code defect. The full pnpm check result was still pending.

Qualified D RESET/OD305 policy and production verifier, typed activation, calendar, legacy and incident release sources remain blocked by R6 and default to missing. S2/P4/R25/JW01 stay OPEN. S3, production, scorecard and merge stay unapproved. Exact-head required CI and canonical backend execution must still run before any separately authorized readiness or merge.
